title: Good as a desk clock but not for travel or as an alarm clock
text:
Good as a desk clock but not for travel or as an alarm clock. In my opinion, this clock is only good as a desk clock and is really not suited as an alarm clock or a travel alarm clock because:

- It is a little larger than typical travel alarm clocks.
- The buttons are on the bottom and will be pressed automatically in the luggage causing the batteries to go dead. There should be something covering them.
- It is awkward to operate.
- One has to turn off the alarm on the bottom of the clock and when half asleep, that button is impossible to see.

FEATURES
- Battery operated (3 AAA batteries NOT included)
- Dual alarm feature (weekdays and weekends or set the same time for both)
- Seven-color selectable back-lit display (red, purple, blue, teal, green, yellow, white/clear)
- Graduated waking feature for alarm with both beeping and lights (initial alarm is one beep, then two, etc.; it cycles through the lights)
- Snooze feature from 5 to 60 minutes
- It has a date feature and 12-hour or 24-hour clock options.

I love the back-lit colors (although they only show when the alarm is on or when the feet or center top is squeezed). I also like the fact that this tells the time and shows the date but I do not like the other features. I was able to set mine to purple but the colors do not stay if the alarm is used. It cycles through all the colors when the alarm goes off and then will stay on the color it cycled to when the alarm was shut off. Setting up this alarm clock was cumbersome. I definitely needed the instructions. What I noticed is that the feet on the clock need to be depressed to engage the snooze alarm. I was unable to get this to work the first time because I had it on a carpeted stair. Therefore, it must be on a hard surface. The fact that I have to locate the snooze button when I am half asleep drove me crazy. I have trouble seeing without my glasses, so that is annoying. Overall, this is a good desk clock only.
